drawio_review_note: Aligned with LAB-Bench arXiv:2407.10362v3 §§2.1–2.4, §§3.1–3.4, Appendix A.1.3, and Supplemental Tables 2–5. Operational evidence is the official Future-House/LAB-Bench repository snapshot 998a8e0a40cf116c80e1b0e7a805ebb5fb9fa838 and Hugging Face dataset revision 5c77cec648430f30611808808861eb86f81d5eaa; repository locators include CloningScenarios/cloningscenarios-v1-splits.json, CloningScenarios/task.py, labbench/zero_shot.py, and labbench/evaluator.py. Cloning Scenarios is a LAB-Bench sub-benchmark, not a standalone paper. Authors and contracted biology experts manually create and revise 41 human-hard, multi-step molecular-cloning MCQs using plasmids, DNA fragments, enzymes, workflow choices, plausible distractors, and an explicit insufficient-information option; related questions may share a scenario but remain independently answerable. The fixed split is exactly 33 public and 8 private questions, with a contamination canary. The paper protocol runs zero-shot chain-of-thought without tools three times, while the pinned harness requests a tagged answer letter and parses it by regex; the insufficient-information choice is treated as unsure. Accuracy is correct/41, Precision is correct/attempted, and Coverage is attempted/41. PhD experts cover all 41 questions with tools allowed but AI prohibited. A separate ten-question open-answer audit reports 2/10 for both Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o, so it is preserved as an audit rather than merged into the MCQ score.
